title: First Conditional
summary: Real future possibilities: 'if + present, will + base'.

theory.markdown:
**First Conditional** describes a *real* future possibility — something that may well happen.

Form:

> **If + Present Simple, will + base verb.**

Examples:
- *If it rains, we'll stay home.*
- *I'll call you if I have time.*

Note: in the *if-clause* we use **present**, even though we're talking about the future. After **will**, use the **base form** (no -s, no to).

items.source: If you study, you will pass.
She will come if you invite her.
If we don't hurry, we'll be late.
items.translation: Jeśli się nie pośpieszymy, spóźnimy się.

exercises.prompt: If it ___ tomorrow, we'll cancel the trip.
If you call me, I ___ (help) you.

answers: If I have time, I will call.
I will call if I have time.
If I have time, I'll call.

exercises.sentence: If she will come, we will start.
answers: If she comes, we will start.
exercises.explanation: No 'will' in the if-clause — use present simple.

exercises.source: It is sunny. We go to the beach.
answers: If it is sunny, we will go to the beach.
If it's sunny, we'll go to the beach.
